scope: Theorem 11.3 (Moving four-change test) of the manuscript “Conformal Limits of Critical Square-Lattice Random-Cluster Interfaces” (preprints/Conformal-Limits-of-Critical-Square-Lattice-Random-Cluster-Interfaces-October-5-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 223 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 b14b09c2088272ae), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 60-61. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let a four-change strand in Vn be stopped before completing its strand, revealing only the switches it has encountered. Let Un be its remaining simple slit disk, with the tip as the new starting mark. Consider histories for which a fixed 60 basepoint has a fixed positive disk in Un, and the four prime-end marks in a disk chart normalized at that basepoint remain mutually separated by a fixed positive amount. Then, on these histories, Popen(EP | Fn) − f(χUn ) −→ 0 in probability. (11.2) Here EP is the primal pairing event, equivalently the actual bridge event after separate primal closure, and χUn is its current ordered cross-ratio. The assertion holds for arbitrary mesh-dependent stopping rules satisfying this localization.
